definitions.label: NoData / Unmapped
definitions.description: Missing orbital elevation or CTX orthomosaic reflectance.

definitions.label: Low-albedo smooth floor facies
definitions.description: Low-slope (<= human limit) terrain with lower CTX 6 m reflectance (< P33).

definitions.label: Intermediate-albedo plains facies
definitions.description: Low-slope (<= human limit) terrain with intermediate CTX 6 m reflectance (P33..P67).

definitions.label: High-albedo etched ridge / bedform facies
definitions.description: Low-slope (<= human limit) terrain with higher CTX 6 m reflectance (> P67).

definitions.label: Moderate slope transition zone (rover/drone)
definitions.description: Moderate slope exceeding human limit (> 10 deg) up to rover limit (<= 20 deg).

definitions.label: Steep scarp / hazard zone (drone only)
definitions.description: Steep slope exceeding rover limit (> 20 deg); surface obstacle.

units.name: Jezero floor unit
units.description: Rugged, moderately-to-heavily cratered, light- to dark-toned, planar unit with margins defined by low-relief, sharp, lobate scarps, forms the central portion of the Jezero crater floor and overlies and embays units Nue and Nle, respectively. Most impact craters on this surface are <200 m. Can have dark, smooth surface texture, especially near contact with unit NHjf2. Type area: lat 18.43°N, long 77.65°E.
units.characteristics: Associated with mafic composition (Goudge and others, 2015). Previously mapped as the 'volcanic floor unit' by Goudge and others (2015).
units.interpretation: Volcanic ash or eolian airfall deposit that drapes underlying topography. Correlates with unit Nnp2 based on common stratigraphic position and shared textural and morphologic characteristics. Emplaced during the Late Noachian before deposition of unit NHjf1. May have been modified by subsequent lacustrine activity during deposition of units NHjf1 and NHjf2. Dark, smooth surface texture near unit NHjf2 is due to a dark mantle deposit or erosional lag derived from erosion of unit NHjf2. Previously interpreted by Schon and others (2012) and Goudge and others (2015) as an extrusive volcanic flow.

units.name: Lower etched unit
units.description: Rugged, lightly cratered, light- to intermediate-toned unit concentrically exposed on the floor of Jezero adjacent to unit Njf. Topographically lower than adjacent unit Nue. Contains NE-SW trending ridges that extend several hundred meters in length. When present, impact craters are typically >200 m in diameter. Type area: lat 18.28°N, long 77.49°E
units.characteristics: Unit is exposed in erosional windows through the overlying unit Njf (for example, 18.44°N, 77.44°E and 18.33°N, 77.73°E). Associated with olivine and variable carbonate (Goudge and others, 2015). Previously mapped as the 'light-toned floor unit' and 'dusty light-toned floor unit' by Goudge and others (2015).
units.interpretation: Volcanic ash deposit, similar to the origin of unit Nue. Could also be other clastic deposit of volcanic or eolian origin. Either deposited into an existing lake within Jezero or subsequently altered by later lacustrine processes during emplacement of units NHjf1 and NHjf2. Underlies unit Nue based on its consistently lower elevation. Ridges are yardangs (Day and Dorn, 2019).
